about.title: Citrus Heights Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Citrus Heights looks different from block to block. Retail crews stock shelves along Sunrise Boulevard, delivery drivers thread Greenback Lane and Antelope Road, and trades workers move between job sites across this Sacramento County city of roughly 87,000 people. When one of those shifts ends in an injury, the path forward usually begins with workers' compensation. California treats comp as the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault, so you do not have to prove anyone did anything wrong to receive medical care and wage benefits. Comp is not always the whole story, though. If a subcontractor, a property owner, a defective piece of equipment, or another driver contributed to what happened, a separate third-party injury claim may exist alongside comp. Driving for work is a common example: Citrus Heights recorded 310 injury collisions in 2025, with 408 people hurt, and some of those involved employees on the clock along Auburn Boulevard. LawProactive connects you, free, with an independent attorney who can sort out which route fits your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Citrus Heights Workers Use LawProactive

items.title: Comp is not always the end of the road
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually your only claim against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or another driver can support a separate injury claim. The attorneys in our network look for that second path.

items.title: Report within 30 days, and know your job is protected
items.desc: California asks you to notify your employer within 30 days of a work injury, and it is illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for doing so. An attorney can help if the report was mishandled or if you faced pushback.

items.title: Two-year deadline, no fee unless you recover
items.desc: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year filing deadline, so timing matters. Our connection service is free, and network attorneys work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Greenback Lane while making deliveries for my employer. Is that a comp claim or a car accident claim?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and a portion of lost wages regardless of who caused the crash. If the other driver was at fault, you may also have a separate third-party claim against that driver, which can address losses comp does not. Citrus Heights saw 408 people injured in collisions during 2025, and on-the-clock drivers are part of that count more often than people expect.

items.question: My supervisor hinted I could lose hours if I filed a comp claim. Is that legal?
items.answer: No. California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report an injury or pursue workers' compensation. Cutting hours, demoting, or firing someone for filing a claim can create additional legal exposure for the employer. If this is happening to you, an attorney can explain your options and help document what occurred.

items.question: How much time do I have after a Citrus Heights work injury?
items.answer: There are two clocks to watch. You should report the injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your workers' compensation benefits. If a third party such as a subcontractor, property owner, or another driver shares responsibility, that separate claim generally must be filed within two years of the injury. Starting early gives an attorney room to gather records before they go missing.
